meta.title: Insider data theft — departing sales engineer
meta.systems: LAPTOP-SE-0412 (sales engineer laptop), SharePoint Online (Sales site), CRM tenant, Exchange Online mailbox, DLP / web proxy
meta.containment: Corporate account suspended and sessions revoked; VPN and CRM export rights removed; personal cloud-storage domain blocked at the proxy; laptop network-isolated by EDR; devices recovered and imaged; cloud copy deleted under counsel supervision and the USB archive hash-matched.
meta.narrative: On 17 February at 08:10 the DLP platform alerted on a 3.8 GB upload from a sales engineer’s VPN session to an uncategorised personal cloud-storage service. The employee had resigned on 2 February to join a competitor. Investigation showed a staged, deliberate collection from 9 February: a bulk download of 212 pricing files, an export of 1,840 EMEA customer contacts from the CRM, three emails forwarded to a personal address, a password-protected archive, a copy to a USB drive and an rclone upload, followed by an attempt to clear traces. The account was suspended within three hours of detection, the laptop was triaged live and then imaged, and HR and counsel led the employee interview. The employee signed an undertaking, the cloud copy was deleted and verified, the USB was returned with a matching archive hash, and the DPO assessed the incident as not reportable under Art. 33. Follow-up actions closed the personal cloud storage gap and linked HR leaver notices to security monitoring.

govern.assets: Sales SharePoint site, CRM tenant, Exchange Online mailbox, LAPTOP-SE-0412, DLP / web proxy
govern.dataTypes: Pricing and discount matrix (trade secret); customer contact records (names, business emails, deal values)
govern.deadlineBasis: UK GDPR Art. 33 — 72h from awareness; assessed as not reportable (risk to individuals unlikely)
govern.legalNotes: Employment law and trade-secret advice via external counsel. Investigation conducted under privilege. Signed undertaking obtained; letter sent to the new employer. No criminal referral.
govern.secureComms: Case discussed only with Legal, HR, CISO and the response team; no discussion with the employee’s line management until after the HR meeting.
govern.bizImpact: No operational outage. Confidential pricing and 1,840 EMEA customer contacts were copied to personal storage and a USB drive and later recovered. Cost is internal IR, HR and legal time; not estimated here.
govern.repRisk: Low — no customer disclosure required; data recovered before use. Competitive risk managed through the undertaking and the letter to the new employer.
govern.insurance: Not a claimable event under the cyber policy. Employment practices cover notified as a precaution.
govern.riskNotes: Residual risk: knowledge retained by the individual. Monitored through contractual obligations and counsel follow-up.

actions.title: Suspend account, revoke sessions and VPN, remove CRM export role
actions.notes: Account disabled in Entra; refresh tokens revoked; VPN profile and CRM export permission removed.

actions.title: Block cloudvault-storage.example at the proxy; isolate laptop via EDR
actions.notes: Domain category set to blocked; laptop network-isolated (management channel left open for live response).

actions.title: Preserve M365 and CRM audit trails (legal hold)
actions.notes: Holds applied; audit retention extended beyond the default window.

actions.title: Instruct external counsel; agree privilege and evidence-handling protocol
actions.notes: Counsel engaged; findings routed through Legal.

actions.title: Remote live-response triage of LAPTOP-SE-0412
actions.notes: USB history, prefetch and browser artefacts collected before the device was recovered.

actions.title: Recover laptop and USB drive; image the laptop with a write blocker
actions.notes: Laptop and the USB drive handed over at the HR meeting. Image hashes verified.

actions.title: Preservation request to the cloud storage provider (via counsel)
actions.notes: Account and access logs preserved pending deletion verification.

actions.title: Factual timeline pack for the HR interview
actions.notes: Neutral timeline with evidence references supplied to HR and Legal.

actions.title: Verify cloud copy deleted and USB returned under signed undertaking
actions.notes: Counsel witnessed deletion; account closed; USB archive hash matched the one on the laptop.

actions.title: Art. 33 UK GDPR risk assessment and decision record
actions.notes: Assessed as unlikely to result in a risk to individuals given recovery and verified deletion. Not reportable; decision documented.

actions.title: Daily check of residual access and sign-ins for the departed account
actions.notes: Daily until end of notice period; no further activity observed.

actions.title: Switch personal cloud-storage categories to block mode
actions.notes: Policy change deployed. Monitor-only mode retired for the personal cloud category.

escalations.reason: Triage confirms confidential pricing IP and 1,840 customer contact records were copied to personal storage and a USB drive. Elevate to high pending recovery.
Cloud copy deleted under counsel supervision, USB recovered and hash-matched, undertaking signed. Residual risk reduced to medium (contractual follow-up).

rootCauses.factor: Personal cloud storage monitored, not blocked
rootCauses.detail: The uncategorised cloud category was set to monitor-only. The DLP alert fired after 3.8 GB had already been uploaded, so detection could not prevent loss.
rootCauses.remediation: Personal and uncategorised cloud-storage categories moved to block mode; exceptions by request. Alert volume threshold lowered.

rootCauses.factor: Resignation not linked to security monitoring
rootCauses.detail: Fifteen days passed between the resignation and detection. HR and Security had no process to raise monitoring on a leaver’s account during their notice period.
rootCauses.remediation: HR now notifies Security on every resignation; leaver watch-list triggers enhanced DLP and unusual-access alerts during notice.

rootCauses.factor: Broad access to pricing and CRM exports
rootCauses.detail: CRM export and the Pricing library were open to all sales users with no sensitivity label or time-limited access. The employee only needed read access to their own accounts.
rootCauses.remediation: CRM export restricted to a managers-only role; Pricing library labelled Confidential with download limited to approved devices.

rootCauses.factor: Removable media permitted on corporate laptops
rootCauses.detail: USB mass storage was allowed with no write-blocking or logging beyond the EDR event stream.
rootCauses.remediation: USB storage set to read-only for standard users; write access by exception with logging.

rootCauses.factor: Managers not primed to report leaver risk
rootCauses.detail: The employee’s manager had noticed unusual evening work in the prior week but had no route or prompt to raise it.
rootCauses.remediation: Managers receive a leaver-risk checklist from HR at resignation, including how to raise concerns to Security.

hostAnalysis.summary: Confirms the staging and exfiltration endpoint. Between 9 and 17 February the user built a 3.8 GB password-protected archive (212 pricing files plus the EMEA customer CSV), copied it to a USB drive on 13 February and, on 16 February, staged portable rclone and a configuration pointing at a personal cloud storage account. CCleaner was run at 22:58 on 16 February to remove traces. The archive was uploaded at 07:55 on 17 February. All activity used the employee’s own account and was visible to the endpoint agent; none of it was blocked.
hostAnalysis.notes: Prefetch shows rclone.exe first run 22:31 on 16 Feb and CCleaner64.exe at 22:58. setupapi.dev.log first entry for the USB serial is 18:22 on 13 Feb. Archive hash matches the copy on the recovered USB. Browser history cleared but the SQLite free pages still hold the cloud-storage login URL. Image mounted read-only; still need to check OneDrive sync folder (clean).

hostAnalysis.summary: The user downloaded 212 files from the Pricing, Contracts and Pipeline libraries in six minutes on the evening of 9 February, after first enumerating the three libraries. The downloads were outside their normal pattern: in the prior 90 days they had opened four files in these libraries. The master price list and discount matrix were included.
hostAnalysis.notes: UAL filtered on user and operation FileDownloaded; 212 events 20:14–20:20. Library enumeration (PageViewed) at 19:52. Baseline: 4 file opens in 90 days. No sharing links created. Access came through the sales-team group with no sensitivity-label restriction.

hostAnalysis.summary: On 11 February at 19:47 the user exported the “All Accounts – EMEA” report (1,840 contacts with names, business emails and deal values) to CSV. The export permission sat in the general sales role. It was the only bulk export the account made in six months.
hostAnalysis.notes: Export size 1,840 rows. Role review: export enabled for all 61 sales users. No scheduled exports. Audit trail retention was due to roll the entry off on 9 March; legal hold placed on 17 Feb.

hostAnalysis.summary: The DLP/proxy captured the upload. A 3.8 GB transfer to an uncategorised personal cloud storage domain began at 07:55 on 17 February from the VPN-authenticated laptop session, using an rclone user-agent. The alert fired at 08:10 once the volume threshold was passed. Policy for the category was monitor-only, so the upload completed.
hostAnalysis.notes: Session start 07:55, ended 08:36. Client egress 203.0.113.88 (residential ISP). Same domain seen once on 16 Feb at 22:40 (test upload of 40 KB). Category: uncategorised → monitor. Confirmed no other users contacted the domain in 30 days.

hostAnalysis.summary: Three emails carrying pricing attachments were forwarded to a personal address on 10 February at 21:18. No mail rule was created and no further forwarding occurred. This is the earliest outbound movement of company data linked to this case.
hostAnalysis.notes: Message trace + item export. Attachments hash-match files in SharePoint (Q1_Pricing_Master_v7.xlsx and two price-book PDFs). Forwarded manually, not via rule. Mailbox audit shows no deletions.

closure.notes: Containment, evidence handling, data recovery, undertaking and notifications complete. Art. 33 decision recorded. Remediation (cloud block, CRM export restriction, leaver feed) deployed. Closed by IR lead with CISO sign-off.

lessons.attendees: Dan H, Priya S, Marcus O, Helena Marsh (CISO), Eleanor Voss (Legal), Raj Patel (DPO), HR Director
lessons.well: DLP raised the alert the same morning and the response was fast: account suspended within three hours and the laptop live-triaged the same day. HR and Legal were engaged before any contact with the employee, which kept the evidence and the process clean. Image hashes matched the recovered USB archive, which made the undertaking enforceable.
lessons.better: Detection came after the data had left. The signs began on 9 February and the resignation was known on 2 February. Monitor-only policy, wide CRM export rights and open USB access made the theft easy and quiet. HR did not feed the leaver into any security process.
lessons.detect: Alert on bulk SharePoint downloads over a baseline; alert on any CRM export by a leaver-watch-list user; alert on portable rclone and CCleaner on managed endpoints; keep USB device-insert alerts for leavers.
lessons.playbook: Add an insider-data-theft playbook: HR and Legal first, then silent monitoring or immediate suspension decision, live-response triage before device recovery, preservation requests, and an Art. 33 assessment checkpoint at 24h.
lessons.training: Manager leaver-risk awareness; analyst refresher on insider-case evidence handling and working under privilege; HR briefing on what Security needs at the point of resignation.
lessons.recs: 1) Block personal cloud storage by default. 2) Restrict CRM export and label the Pricing library. 3) Automate an HR-to-Security leaver feed with enhanced monitoring for the notice period. 4) Make USB storage read-only for standard users. 5) Publish the insider-data-theft playbook and run a tabletop within the quarter.
